LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to process with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`. 

Key observations:
- The source array contains three entries: a GitHub releases tarball (normal), a git repository for tdlib (with SKIP checksum, which is standard and permitted for VCS sources), and a patch file reference. All are legitimate source definitions.
- The SHA256 checksum for the first source is present and valid; the second (git source) has "SKIP" which is explicitly allowed per AUR packaging standards for VCS sources.
- The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions contain code that would execute during normal `makepkg` runs, but these are protected by the `--nobuild --noprepare` flags — neither will run during this audit phase.
- There is no malicious code, obfuscation, or unexpected file operations in the visible code. The git URL points to the official tdlib repository, which is the correct source for the telegram-tdlib dependency.
- The only "non-standard" element is the SKIP checksum on the git source, but this is explicitly documented as a normal practice in AUR packaging (SKIP is REQUIRED for VCS sources). The full PKGBUILD review will still capture this as a potential issue, but it does not make the file unsafe for the narrow gate defined.

Since the commands only fetch sources (which writes files but doesn't execute them) and parse the PKGBUILD (without running any functions), and none of these actions involve executing untrusted code or performing unauthorized network requests outside the package's own sources, the file is SAFE for this specific audit gate.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The PKGBUILD is safe for `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` — it contains only legitimate source definitions (GitHub releases and tdlib git repo with a standard SKIP checksum) and no malicious code or unexpected operations.</summary>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe to run with `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The top-level scope contains only standard PKGBUILD variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `depends`, `makedepends`, etc.), a `source` array declaration, and `sha256sums` array declaration. The only top-level command is `: ${_use_sodeps:=false}`, which is a benign parameter expansion to default the `_use_sodeps` variable to `false`.

The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are defined but will not be executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so any code within them is out of scope for this narrow gate. (Note: the `package()` function does contain an `eval` statement, but it only runs when `_use_sodeps` is true during actual packaging — it is not relevant here.)

The source URLs point to the package's own declared upstream (`github.com/Forkgram/tdesktop`) and the official `tdlib/td` repository. The SKIPped checksum on the git source is expected and required for VCS sources.
</details>
<evidence>
